findings.title: DMARC not enforced (p=none): domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud

evidence.excerpt: DMARC record: v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc@brightwaterfleet.example; policy none, pct 100.

findings.deal_impact: Domain can be spoofed for BEC/wire fraud, increasing payment-fraud and phishing risk and potentially affecting cyber-insurance terms.

remediation.summary: Move DMARC from p=none to quarantine then reject, monitoring rua reports and aligning all senders.

findings.title: SPF uses soft/neutral fail

evidence.excerpt: SPF record: v=spf1 include:_spf.mailhost.example include:sendgrid.example ~all; qualifier ~all.

findings.deal_impact: Softfail weakens spoofing controls and compounds the DMARC p=none exposure for impersonation campaigns.

remediation.summary: Inventory authorized senders, then change SPF from ~all to -all once legitimate mail is confirmed.

findings.title: DNSSEC not enabled

evidence.excerpt: DNSSEC enabled: false on DS query for brightwaterfleet.example.

findings.deal_impact: Unprotected DNS increases spoofing/redirection risk; low standalone deal impact but easy hygiene gap to close.

remediation.summary: Enable DNSSEC at registrar/DNS provider and validate DS publication.

findings.title: Publicly logged hostnames suggest exposed admin/legacy/staging systems

evidence.excerpt: Risky hostname pattern vpn; first_seen 2023-02-11, last_seen 2026-09-30.
Risky hostname pattern jenkins|old; first_seen 2021-06-03, last_seen 2026-08-14.
Risky hostname pattern staging; first_seen 2024-01-20, last_seen 2026-10-01.
Risky hostname pattern legacy; first_seen 2019-11-05, last_seen 2026-07-22.

findings.deal_impact: CT logs suggest exposed VPN/admin/legacy/staging systems that expand attack surface and may need remediation or decommissioning post-close.

remediation.summary: Validate ownership and exposure of risky hosts, decommission legacy/staging or place admin/VPN behind strong access controls.

findings.title: Large certificate footprint relative to company size

evidence.excerpt: unique_hostnames: 47, risky_hostnames_count: 4, exceeding the >40 sprawl threshold for a 201-1000 employee company.

findings.deal_impact: 47 hostnames suggest asset-inventory sprawl, complicating patching and ownership assurance during diligence.

remediation.summary: Reconcile CT hostnames to an authoritative asset inventory and remove orphaned certificates/hosts.

findings.title: Deprecated TLS versions offered

evidence.excerpt: tls_support TLSv1.0: true, TLSv1.1: true, TLSv1.2: true; tls_versions [TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2].

findings.deal_impact: www host offers deprecated TLS, weakening transport security and indicating inconsistent web hardening versus the apex host.

remediation.summary: Disable TLSv1.0 and TLSv1.1 on www, retaining TLSv1.2+ with modern ciphers.

findings.title: HSTS not set

evidence.excerpt: Header strict-transport-security: null on apex host.
Header strict-transport-security: null on www host.

findings.deal_impact: Missing HSTS allows downgrade to insecure HTTP on first visits; minor cost but signals web hardening gaps.

remediation.summary: Set strict-transport-security header on apex and www after confirming HTTPS readiness.

findings.title: Internet-facing appliance listed in CISA KEV (version not verified)

evidence.excerpt: KEV match CVE-PLACEHOLDER-0001, ExampleGate SSL-VPN version 7.0.11, match_tier appliance_exposed, product-level only; version not verified. KEV snapshot 2026-10-20.
Fingerprint ExampleGate SSL-VPN 7.0.11, kind appliance, source asset_path on www host.

findings.deal_impact: Potential exposure: internet-facing ExampleGate SSL-VPN is product-matched to CISA KEV (version not verified); requires urgent patch-level confirmation and could affect insurability if exploitable.

remediation.summary: Immediately verify appliance version/patch against KEV CVE, patch or restrict access, and review VPN logs for exploitation.

findings.title: Publicly disclosed security incident in the last 24 months

evidence.excerpt: State AG breach notice dated 2025-08-14: unauthorized access to a customer support system; approx. 3,100 individuals notified. disclosed_within_months: 14; entity_match exact.

findings.deal_impact: Recent disclosed breach (14 months ago, ~3,100 notified) raises regulatory, customer-trust, and insurance disclosure questions for the deal.

remediation.summary: Obtain incident report, remediation evidence, regulator/customer notification status, and confirm closure/lessons learned.

deal_recommendations.text: Make signing conditional on verification of the internet-facing appliance version and patch level and completion of a compromise assessment, scheduled in Days 0–30 and consistent with full cyber diligence before signing [F-008].
Commission a scope review of the KEV-listed appliance exposure as part of the escalated diligence before signing, covering patch status, access restrictions and VPN log review in Days 0–30 [F-008].

Seek protection for pre-closing incident losses arising from the disclosed incident, with the incident file and closure evidence to be obtained in Days 31–60 in line with diligence before signing [F-009].

Assume the known disclosed incident is likely to be excluded from representations and warranties coverage and structure the transaction accordingly, completing the related review in Days 31–60 under the pre-signing diligence escalation [F-009].

Confirm cyber insurability and any underwriting requirements before close, because unenforced DMARC may affect terms, with remediation planned for Days 31–60 and diligence escalated before signing [F-001].

Require completion of the remaining remediation as a post-close covenant, spanning Days 31–60 for DMARC and incident closure, Days 61–100 for SPF, risky-host and TLS work, and the escalated pre-signing diligence position [F-001] [F-002] [F-004] [F-006] [F-009].

No price adjustment is warranted, as total remediation of $80K–$388K is immaterial relative to the 50M-250M revenue band, with work phased from Days 0–30 through After day 100 alongside full diligence before signing [F-001] [F-008] [F-009].

narrative.executive_summary:
Bottom line: Full cyber diligence is required before signing [F-008] [F-009]. Brightwater scored 71.6 with a C rating, capped by a critical, potentially exploitable exposure [F-008] and a publicly disclosed incident within 24 months [F-009].

Key risks: An internet-facing appliance is product-matched to a known exploited vulnerability, with version not verified [F-008]. A disclosed incident raises regulatory, customer-trust and insurance questions [F-009]. The domain can be spoofed for payment fraud and phishing because email authentication is not enforced [F-001] [F-002]. Publicly suggested admin, legacy and staging hosts expand the attack surface [F-004].

Management credibility: The input records 0 contradictions, with 0 contradicted, 0 unsupported and 0 supported claims, and no management interview was provided to test explanations [F-009].

Next steps: Verify the appliance and review for exploitation in the earliest remediation window [F-008], obtain incident closure evidence in the following window [F-009], and confirm insurability before close [F-001] [F-009].
